evidence: The assertion matched one spelling of one writer in the function source and never invoked enactSwitch at all, so any indirect or renamed write passed it; the fix stubs eleven fs write entry points and runs all four choices end to end.
guidance_note: A test that asserts on a function's source text asserts nothing about behaviour - stub the effect and run the code instead.

evidence: switch-request.js re-implemented the split-on-newline plus trailing-empty pop that laws-excise's run() and applyRequest() already performed, with only a comment claiming the numbering agrees; 13de7cd exported toRawLines and routed all three callers through it.
guidance_note: When you write a comment asserting two copies must stay in step, export the rule instead of the comment.

evidence: The snapshot is read after rewindConversationTo runs, so for rewind_discard the rebuilt array equals it and changed reported false immediately after a destructive truncation; 13de7cd's diff confirms the split into replaces and changed = plan.rewindAt !== null || replaces.
guidance_note: When a return value reports what an operation did, test the report on every branch, including the one whose only effect happens before the value is computed.

evidence: seam-registry.js exports snapshotOf and its own suite asserts callers cannot spell it differently, yet switch-request.js inlined controller.transcript.getSnapshot() - the one call site defeating a guarantee the tests claim to hold.
guidance_note: Before opening a PR, grep for the inline spelling of any fact a module exports an accessor for, and fix every hit in one pass.

evidence: Strict equality against an undefined uuid matches every message that carries no uuid field, so ownerOf(undefined) would return a wrongly-proven owner; the agent refused the reviewer's suggestion to reuse UNOWNED.none and added a distinct noUuid reason, which keeps two different diagnoses apart.
guidance_note: An identity lookup should refuse an absent identifier by name rather than let it match the records that also lack one.

evidence: The registrar pushed a strong reference per controller with no removal path, pinning every announced conversation's message array for the life of the process in a file whose own header says subagent controllers are routine; the fix holds WeakRefs and proves collection by re-execing with --expose-gc.
guidance_note: A registry the app never tells you to empty needs its holding strength decided when it is written, not after a reviewer names the leak.

evidence: summaryFrom builds the appended summary by spreading the found template, so with a craft load as the only user-typed record the user's preserved summary inherited isMeta and would be treated as injected non-chat content; 13de7cd added the !m.isMeta exclusion and rewrote the test that had blessed the craft load as a valid template.
guidance_note: When a function shapes its output by spreading a found record, the search predicate is the contract - enumerate which records must not be found.

evidence: onRecord is async and invoked fire-and-forget from the data handler, so a throw out of encode escaped both the JSON.parse try and the onRequest try and became an unhandled rejection inside the hosted session - the outcome the adjacent comment promises cannot happen; the fix guards the whole body and asserts no unhandledRejection fires.
guidance_note: An async callback invoked without await has no catch above it - guard its whole body, not the single call you were thinking about.

evidence: applyLiveSwitch drives controller.rewindConversationTo before any later step can throw, so the-switch-threw returns with the conversation already truncated while the CLI printed 'Nothing was changed'; atomicity was genuinely unavailable, and the agent stopped the claim rather than faking a rollback.
guidance_note: A user-facing claim about what was changed must be derived from what the code can prove, not from the fact that an error came back.

evidence: On a spawn failure Node leaves status null and stderr empty, so the not-zero branch fired and printed an empty parenthesis; the agent verified the branch is worse than described and added the error.message then 'no output' fallback.
guidance_note: When branching on a child process's exit status, handle the case where it never started - a null status with empty stderr is a distinct outcome from a non-zero exit.

evidence: bin/laws-switch already derived its accepted choices from Object.keys(SWITCH_ACTIONS) while live-switch.js re-listed the four by hand, so a fifth action would have been accepted by the CLI and refused live as unknownChoice; 13de7cd's diff replaces the literal with the derivation.
guidance_note: When one consumer already derives an enum from its owner, no second consumer gets to re-list it.

evidence: transform is the only path by which the spliced seam reaches the compiler, the runtime suite's build() never passed one, and the failure mode is silent - the registrar simply never fires; the fix added five cases including the swapped-argument case that an identity transform would hide.
guidance_note: A new parameter that is the sole wire for a feature needs a test at the seam it is wired through, not only on the unit that produces its value.

evidence: new RegExp(source, 'gg') does throw, and bun-host.mjs calls resolveSeams with no try/catch, so the crash bypasses the eager-resolution fallback the design exists for; seam-plan.js is not among 13de7cd's changed files, so the fix-commit flag is a false positive - this is original-PR code round 0 never reached. The reviewer's aside that 'y' cannot combine with 'g' is wrong and the agent adopted the y-strip without checking it, though it is harmless here.
guidance_note: When composing a regex from a declared one, normalise the flags at the point of composition instead of assuming what future declarations will carry.

evidence: F6's fix made the targets weak but left announced append-only, so the backing array still grew for the life of the process and every count/ownerOf scanned entries that can never resolve; the agent compacted in live() and proved the length falls after collection.
guidance_note: A weak-reference fix is half a leak fix - the container holding the refs needs its own compaction decided in the same pass.

evidence: 13de7cd wrapped the server's encode(response) for F8 and left the client's encode(request) inside a plain connect listener in the same file, where a throw is uncaught and kills the laws-switch process; the agent said so himself - symmetric to the server-side fix that he did not carry across.
guidance_note: When guarding one end of a symmetric protocol, fix both ends in the same commit - the file is the unit, not the call site.

evidence: The equivalent-mutant note did exist at the finish latch, so the reviewer's claim that no comment names it was wrong in letter, but it used none of the words the ledger sends a reader to grep for, which is the defect the agent fixed by rewording the comment rather than weakening the ledger. SEAMS.md is not in 13de7cd's file list, so the fix-commit flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: A document that tells a reader to go find something in the source must name it in the words that reader will actually search for.

evidence: 13de7cd imported snapshotOf into switch-request.js for F4 and, in the same commit, rewrote applyLiveSwitch's tail for F3 while leaving controller.transcript.getSnapshot() inline six lines above the edited region.
guidance_note: After fixing a one-source violation at one call site, grep the whole change for the same expression before declaring the finding closed.

evidence: For rewind_summarize the rewind lands at loadIndex+1, so every non-anchor conflict is newer and is deleted by the cut regardless of whether it was stubbable, yet the loop refused the whole plan - the same reasoning the file already applied to rewind_discard two lines above. live-switch.js's tombstone loop is untouched by 13de7cd, so the fix-commit flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: When a comment explains why one branch may skip a requirement, check every other branch the same reasoning covers.

evidence: The live path aimed the rewind at snapshot[loadIndex] with no loadIndex zero guard while laws-excise's disk rewind_discard hard-refuses that state, so the two enforcers disagreed and the live one would truncate the conversation to empty; the flagged branch is original-PR code, and the fix even exposed a fixture that had been sitting in that state.
guidance_note: When a live path re-implements a decision the disk path already enforces, enumerate the disk path's refusals and match them one for one.

evidence: F8's fix introduced THREW and UNENCODABLE as the named group of server-originated reasons and left the third server-originated failure, the server's onMalformed, still answering with the client-facing UNREACHABLE.malformed - visible as unchanged context in 13de7cd's diff directly below the lines it edited.
guidance_note: When a fix creates a named category of failure, sweep every existing failure that belongs in the category rather than only the one that prompted it.

evidence: JSON.stringify returns undefined rather than throwing for undefined, a function or a symbol, so the try/catch F8's fix added let the literal text undefined onto the wire and the failure resurfaced at the far end as a generic parse error; the agent fixed encode itself, which both directions pass through, rather than the single call site the reviewer named.
guidance_note: A try/catch is not a guard for a function that signals failure by returning a value - enumerate both failure shapes when you wrap a call.

evidence: liveIndexOf compares the same m.uuid field that F5's ownerOf fix guarded, and non-anchor conflict uuids never pass through ownerOf, so an absent uuid would match the first record that also lacks one; the guard was fixed in one identity lookup and not the other in the same round.
guidance_note: When an ambiguity is fixed in one identity lookup, fix every identity lookup in the change that compares the same field.

evidence: The comment naming seam-plan.test.mjs is an added line inside the transform-test block that 13de7cd wrote as F12's fix, and the file that exists is seam-plan.test.js.
guidance_note: A filename written into a comment is checkable - check it as you write it.

evidence: laws-excise.js's ALL FOUR ARE ON-DISK TRANSCRIPT SURGERY block asserts that claude's native rewind is never driven, which the PR's own live-switch.js refutes by calling rewindConversationTo; the block predates every fix commit, so this is drift from the original change rather than from a fix, and the citation is apt because the fix shrank the block from eleven lines to four.
guidance_note: When a change makes a claim elsewhere in the repo false, the sweep for that claim belongs in the same commit as the change.

evidence: F9's fix made the CLI's wording reason-specific for the-switch-threw alone and left timeout and malformed on the generic 'Nothing was changed' arm, which is the same lie; the agent then found that noSocket itself was doing double duty and split off noAnswer, so only a connection that never opened may claim nothing happened.
guidance_note: When a claim is false for one reason code, enumerate the whole reason set against the claim instead of special-casing the one that was named.

evidence: bin/laws-switch grew a live-versus-relaunch fork, a retire-craft loop with two distinct failure arms and reason-specific messaging with no test file anywhere in the tree; most of that logic arrived in the original commit, so the fix-commit flag is largely a false positive, though 13de7cd did add further untested branching to the same file.
guidance_note: A CLI that grows branching and failure arms gets its own suite in the commit that adds them, driven as a subprocess against a stub peer.

evidence: The status ledger named two enacting choices while the RESOLVED section directly above it concluded all three were verified live; SEAMS.md is absent from 13de7cd's file list, so the drift came from af5d4d9 recording the third verification without updating the summary layer.
guidance_note: When a document has a summary layer and a detail layer, update both in the commit that adds the detail.

evidence: Before F6's WeakRef change an empty live set could only mean the seam never fired; afterwards every controller being collected reports the same neverAnnounced, collapsing the distinction the count getter's own comment promises, and an existing test had already written that conflation down as an expectation. The agent added a never-reset everAnnounced latch and a separate allEnded reason.
guidance_note: When a change makes an empty state newly reachable, re-read every message and test that was written on the assumption it was not.

evidence: toRawLines was created by F2's fix as the single splitting rule for three callers and shipped with no direct test - only applyRequest round trips that always use exactly one trailing newline; the reviewer's if-to-while regression would have passed everything, and the agent's own note records that his first expectation for a lone newline was wrong while the code was right.
guidance_note: A helper extracted to be a single source of truth is new public surface - give it direct cases for its edges in the commit that extracts it.

evidence: The anchor regex is the single string tying the whole mechanism to the app's real source and its only check was a one-time manual run against a live binary, with an over-broad match failing unsafely rather than refusing; seams.js appears in none of the fix commits, so this is original-PR code the reviewer took until round 2 to reach.
guidance_note: The literal that ties a mechanism to an external system gets a test against a recorded sample of that system, not a manual verification recorded in prose.

evidence: enactSwitch read the caller-supplied transcript path and never looked at pending.json, and the sessionId the CLI sends was accepted and ignored, so a same-privilege process could name any file and drive rewind_summarize with attacker-authored text appended as an ordinary non-meta user message - defeating the safety claim switch-channel.js's own docstring makes. The agent bound the request to the offer, corrected the docstring rather than propping it up, and ran the attack live, which exposed a second defect: the offer was never consumed, so one offer could be enacted twice.
guidance_note: When a docstring claims a capability bound, name the code that enforces it - an unenforced safety claim is itself the defect.

evidence: The reject branch and its hardcoded no-op literal were introduced in b02acff, an unrequested mid-review commit that fixed a self-found bug, duplicating applyLiveSwitch's return shape for exactly one of four choices; caused_by is null because no earlier finding's fix produced it - the flag is right about the timing and there is no earlier finding to name. The reviewer offered a sync comment or a shared helper and the agent took the helper.
guidance_note: When a new branch reproduces another function's return shape, export the shape rather than retyping it.

evidence: Same defect as F31 reported at a different line of the same function, and the agent explicitly treated the two threads as one; the hole itself came from the original commit, so the post-review-commit flag reflects only b02acff's edits to the surrounding lines.

bin/laws-switch.test.js was added by e82f4c2 as F26's fix and leaked two temp directories per case - the agent counted 3891 accumulated locally, so the reviewer's 'indefinitely' was literal; rather than the proposed second tracking list he collapsed WORK, bed() and the hand-rolled case onto one temp() helper with one registry, which is why the law citation fits.
guidance_note: A test file added to close a finding is new code - give every resource it creates one creation path and one cleanup.

evidence: socket.setEncoding('utf8') makes the buffer a decoded string, so buffer.length counts UTF-16 code units against a constant named MAX_RECORD_BYTES and CJK content passes roughly three times the intended bound. The cap was added in b02acff as unrequested hardening rather than as any finding's fix, and 8d5b40f changed only this file's header docstring, so the named-fix-commit flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: When a bound is named in bytes, measure bytes where they accumulate - a decoded string's length is a different unit than the one the name promises.

evidence: The close arm settled through finish() and skipped clearTimeout while error, connect and the reader all settled through done(); the reviewer correctly said the settled latch absorbs the late firing so there is no observable bug. The line is present in the original f35b708 and e82f4c2 changed only its reason field, so no fix caused it, and the citation is apt because the change removes an arm rather than adding one.
guidance_note: When a helper exists to settle a promise, every arm settles through it - an exception is a second spelling of the same step.

evidence: handleRestoreMessage does not contain restoreMessageSync at all - capital R and no Sync - so the case returned the empty list trivially and covered neither the word-character nor the dollar arm of the lookbehind, which is the over-broad direction the file's own header calls the dangerous one; seams.test.js was added by 8d5b40f as F30's fix, and the agent's mutation check confirms a narrowed lookbehind would have passed under the old case.
guidance_note: An exclusion test must contain the string it claims to exclude - prove the input matches without the guard before asserting it does not with it.

evidence: IDLE_MS was hardcoded inside createSwitchServer while maxBytes and timeoutMs are parameters precisely so a test can shorten them, and the only related assertion bounded the constant's value rather than exercising the disconnect. The idle timeout arrived in b02acff as unrequested hardening, not as any finding's fix, so the named-fix-commit flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: A deadline or limit added for resource protection is only testable if it crosses the boundary as a value - parameterise it in the commit that adds it.

evidence: consumeOffer was added by 8d5b40f as the single-use-offer half of F31's fix, and its bare catch swallows EACCES or EBUSY as readily as ENOENT, leaving the offer on disk after the switch has already been applied live and reopening the exact replay the fix was built to close. The agent narrowed to ENOENT, reported the rest on the boot channel, and stated plainly that the fix has no test because bun-host.mjs has no suite.
guidance_note: A catch written for one errno must test for that errno - a bare catch in a consume step silently restores the state the step exists to destroy.

narrative: Thirty-nine findings over four rounds on a large new injector feature; the agent accepted essentially all of them, and the four times it varied the fix (F5, F16, F21, F34) the variation was better than what the reviewer proposed. Thirteen findings exist because of an earlier fix: four are the same gap left standing at a second call site in the same file (F15, F17, F20, F22), four are defects inside code a fix commit added (F23, F34, F37, F39), three are gaps in the new guard or helper a fix introduced (F14, F21, F29), and two are states a fix newly made reachable (F25, F28). Round 3 is the avoidable one - four of its six findings are bugs inside earlier fixes and the other two sit on hardening the agent added mid-review without being asked. Against that, the reviewer took until rounds 2 and 3 to reach two of the original commit's worst defects, the untested anchor regex (F30) and the unbound switch channel (F31/F33), so not every extra round was the agent's to save.
guidance_observations: Every fix commit shipped at least one defect the next round found - 13de7cd produced F14, F15, F17, F20, F21, F22, F23 and F25; e82f4c2 produced F34; 8d5b40f produced F37 and F39 - so the fix diff never received the sweep the original diff received.

The commonest single cause is a one-call-site fix in a two-call-site file: after fixing a duplication, a missing guard or a renamed reason, grep the change for the same expression before replying Fixed.

Introducing a named category - server-originated reasons, weak references, a single-use offer, a shared splitter - reliably produced the next round's finding, because the category was applied to the instance that prompted it rather than swept across the file it lives in.

Three findings (F32, F35, F38) landed on unrequested hardening bundled into mid-review commits, which is review surface the agent added to itself while under review and a distinct cost from incomplete fixes.

The agent's reply discipline was not the failure: every thread carries a plan, a named fix commit and, on the security thread, a live attack run that found a second defect his unit tests had missed - what was missing was treating each fix commit as new code with its own review scope.
